app.title: Large Spreadsheet Analyzer
language.label: Language
step.file.title: Choose file
step.file.help: Select the spreadsheet you want to analyze. Supported formats: CSV, XLS, XLSX and ODS. Files of several hundred MB are fine.
step.import.title: Import options
step.import.help: Check how the file will be read. For CSV files, verify the separator, encoding and header settings with the preview.
step.rules.title: Define rules
step.rules.help: Each rule finds rows to fix, independently of the other rules. Add conditions and combine them with AND / OR. You can save rules to a JSON file and load them again later.
step.run.title: Run
step.run.help: Start the scan. The file is read once and every rule is evaluated on each row. You can cancel at any time and keep partial results.
step.report.title: Report
step.report.help: Review the matches of each rule, page through sample rows, and export the results.
file.memory_warning: XLS and ODS files cannot be read row by row: the whole sheet is loaded into memory. Very large files may be slow or run out of memory - consider converting to CSV or XLSX first.
csv.dialog.title: CSV import options
csv.preview.error: Cannot read the file with these settings: {error}

rules.empty: No rules defined yet. Add a rule or load a rules file.
rules.need_one: Define at least one rule before continuing.

step.dupfile.title: Duplicate file
step.dupfile.help: Generate a CSV of duplicate rows to remove. Select a reference file and map its columns to the scanned file. In each duplicate group, rows with identical right-hand cells keep only the lowest ID; unique rows are kept only when an identical row exists in the reference file.
dupfile.no_rule: This scan has no 'is duplicated in several rows' rule - there is nothing to extract here.
dupfile.done: {written} duplicate row(s) extracted; {kept} row(s) kept; {groups} group(s) processed; reference: {reference} row(s).
dupfile.cancelled: Extraction cancelled - the file is incomplete.
step.verify.title: Verification
step.verify.help: Every row of the generated duplicate file is checked again: condition A means its content (key columns plus everything to their right) appears several times in the original file; condition B means it appears exactly once and is missing from the reference file. INVALID rows should not have been extracted.
verify.no_data: Extract and save a duplicate file first - there is nothing to verify yet.
verify.summary: {total} row(s) verified: {valid_a} valid (condition A), {valid_b} valid (condition B), {invalid} INVALID.
